animal_sacred_grove.title: Sacred Grove
animal_sacred_grove.text: Yaksha-marked trees and colored ropes wound around ancient root systems indicate the boundaries of this place. The grove has been tended so long it breathes on its own — the leaves move when nothing else does. Yaksha and Yakshini commune with followers here in the old way: no temples, no intermediaries, just the practitioners and the inhabited earth beneath their feet.

outcome.text: A Yakshini turns and regards you without surprise. Earth magic has a price — she names it.
You walk on. The light here filters differently than the rest of the forest — warmer, somehow, as though the sun is paying attention.

animal_temple_of_the_naga.title: Temple of the Naga
animal_temple_of_the_naga.text: Offerings of saffron-milk and wild flowers line the path to the shrine — fresh, which means someone was here recently. The naga temple here is older than the settlements that surround it, and the naga who receive worship here are older still. Their presence is felt as a weight in the air, like the moment before rain.

outcome.text: A practitioner rises smoothly and names the spells they can teach. The price is gold. The naga do not haggle.

choices.text: Move on without disturbing the offerings

outcome.text: You don't touch the flowers. The scent of saffron and something older follows you for a while.

animal_garuda_roost.title: Garuda Roost
animal_garuda_roost.text: A horned pole rises from the high ground — above the canopy where it can be seen from the air, or from a cliff edge visible to anything that flies. The garudas pass through this realm regularly on their circuits between worlds. Followers of all species gather here to wait, to offer, and sometimes to receive teachings when the great birds land. Shyena and kapota are among the most devoted.

outcome.text: One of the worshippers looks up. They teach Air magic here. The price is negotiable, but only within reason.
You set something at the base of the pole and move on. The ribbons flutter.

animal_hidden_gompa.title: Hidden Gompa
animal_hidden_gompa.text: A structure of woven branches and packed earth, half-reclaimed by the forest. Inside, mantric syllables are audible — not quite human in their cadence, adjusted over years of practice to harmonize with birdsong and the sounds of the forest. Monks who withdrew from the human realm into the animal realm for solitude. They have been here a long time. The animals have grown accustomed to them.

outcome.text: After a pause, the door opens. A monk gestures you inside. Space magic. What do you need?
You walk past quietly. The mantras continue without interruption.

animal_medicinal_garden.title: Medicinal Garden
animal_medicinal_garden.text: A clearing carved from the forest floor, every inch cultivated with medicinal plants. Some healers here were born in these forests; others retreated from human settlements to practice more freely. The knowledge is older than any of them — root-knowledge, bark-knowledge, the deep grammar of the healing forest. The teachers share it openly, for a fee.

outcome.text: A healer looks up from her work and nods. She names her price without ceremony.
You leave without disturbing them. The scent of growing things follows you for some time.

animal_black_lodge.title: Black Lodge
animal_black_lodge.text: The entrance is low, partially hidden by undergrowth. You would miss it if you were not looking. Inside: incense so thick it stings, a khatvanga propped against the wall streaming black ribbons. The practitioner here works alone, without students, without oversight — the animal realm affords the privacy that the human realm did not. They turn when you enter, without surprise.

outcome.text: A hand gestures to a list scratched into the bark of the wall. Spells. Prices. No preamble.
You step back into the daylight. The khatvanga watches you leave.

animal_yogini_circle.title: Circle of the Yoginis
animal_yogini_circle.text: A ring of standing stones in a forest clearing or on a meadow hill — no ceiling, built that way intentionally so the witches can land when they fly in from the sky. The sixty-four forms are inscribed on the inner face of each stone in a script that predates the current tradition of inscription. Practitioners who come here have traveled a long way to reach this circle.

outcome.text: One of the practitioners turns and gestures. No words needed.
You back away slowly. The air around the circle hums for a long time after.

animal_mirror_lake.title: Mirror Lake
animal_mirror_lake.text: A lake so still it seems to reflect a different sky — no wind reaches it, or the water ignores the wind. Enchantment practitioners gather at the shore to meditate on appearance and reality. In a realm where a deer's world and a wolf's world overlap in the same territory and neither sees what the other sees, the question has obvious urgency.

outcome.text: A practitioner meets your eyes in the reflection before turning around. They can teach Enchantment. The lake makes everything seem like a fair price.

choices.text: Walk away from the still water

outcome.text: You step back. The image on the water holds for a moment longer than it should, then dissolves.

animal_crossroads_stupa.title: Crossroads Stupa
animal_crossroads_stupa.text: Where the old game trails intersect, someone built a stupa centuries ago. The mortar between the stones includes offerings pressed in during construction — seeds, feathers, a cracked egg. Butter lamps burn at the base. The place smells of juniper smoke and something that has been burning for a very long time.

outcome.text: A practitioner emerges from behind the stupa. Summoning magic — the crossroads is the right place for it. Gold is the price.
You watch the butter lamps in the wind. Some things are better left undisturbed.

animal_eternal_fire.title: Temple of the Eternal Fire
animal_eternal_fire.text: The fire burns at the entrance to a cave, or near a volcanic vent, or at the base of an ancient tree struck by lightning and somehow still alive — wherever the ground produces heat that can be consecrated. The priests who tend it wear white and speak rarely. Creatures of many species come to pay respects. The fire does not discriminate.

outcome.text: A priest turns from the flame and regards you. He names the spells, and then the prices.
You bow before the flame and step back. The fire reflected in your eyes for some time after.

animal_ocean_teahouse.title: Tide Shelter
animal_ocean_teahouse.text: A structure built into a sea cliff, half-submerged at high tide and bone-dry at low. A fire burns in a sealed alcove. Along the benches: naga, karka, and silhouettes you don't immediately place. The keeper is a broad and unhurried makara current who settled down forty years ago and has been pouring the same tea blend since. Nobody asks the recipe.

outcome.text: You take a seat. The current sets down a cup without asking.
You keep going. The smell of salt and smoke follows you out of the cliff.

animal_forest_teahouse.title: Forest Teahouse
animal_forest_teahouse.text: A platform structure high in the canopy, reachable by rope bridges from three directions. The vanara who run it have been doing so since before any of them can remember. The tea is brewed from forest herbs you don't recognize and tastes like rain, bark, and something that is not quite spice. It is very good.

outcome.text: You take a platform seat. A vanara sets down cups without ceremony.
The smell of forest tea follows you along the rope bridge.

animal_meadow_teahouse.title: Watering Hole Teahouse
animal_meadow_teahouse.text: A low structure at the edge of the great watering hole, where the land slopes gently down to the water. The truce of thirst holds here — every creature in the meadow observes it, because the keeper enforces it, and the keeper has been here longer than any of them. Inside: food, drink, and improbable peace.

outcome.text: You take a table. Nobody challenges you. This is the truce.
You walk past the watering hole without stopping. The smell of water and cooking carries far on open ground.

animal_ocean_mercenary_guild.title: Mercenary Guild
animal_ocean_mercenary_guild.text: A fortified reef structure flying a plain banner — the same universal mercenary symbol, translated into something that can survive salt water. Inside, armed figures clean weapons or sleep. The work available in the ocean is different from the work available on land, and the going rate reflects the depth.

outcome.text: The quartermaster produces a list. Rates, availability, terms.
You leave the mercenaries to their maintenance.

animal_forest_mercenary_guild.title: Mercenary Guild
animal_forest_mercenary_guild.text: A fortified outpost at the forest edge, flying a plain black banner between two old trees. The figures inside are armoured in hide and shell-plate — practical for the terrain. They look up when you enter with the universal expression of people who do this professionally.

outcome.text: The quartermaster opens a case and waits.
You leave the mercenaries to their sharpening.

animal_meadow_mercenary_guild.title: Mercenary Guild
animal_meadow_mercenary_guild.text: A stockaded compound at a crossroads of migration routes, flying the universal mercenary banner on a pole tall enough to be seen from a distance. Inside, armoured figures play dice and argue rates. The work in the open meadow is the most visible and the most dangerous, and the prices reflect that.

outcome.text: The quartermaster nods and produces a list. Standard rates. Meadow surcharge.
You skirt the compound and keep moving.

animal_ocean_training_camp.title: Naga Training Grounds
animal_ocean_training_camp.text: A reef plateau where naga warriors train daily — the drills are ancient and precise. They accept outsiders who show genuine commitment. The water here slows everything and makes every technique twice as demanding, which is the point.

outcome.text: A senior naga warrior looks you over once. 'Two sessions. Choose carefully.'
The drills continue without you.

animal_forest_training_camp.title: Tracker's Training Ground
animal_forest_training_camp.text: A clearing used by those who hunt without being hunted — trackers, scouts, the nimble-fingered and the quick-footed. The vanara here share techniques that have been refined over many generations in this specific forest. Some of it translates; all of it is worth knowing.

outcome.text: A vanara elder with patient eyes names two skills. 'Which two? Choose once.'
You leave the clearing. The forest returns to its own lesson.

animal_meadow_training_camp.title: Open-Field Training Ground
animal_meadow_training_camp.text: A camp at the edge of the open plain where fighters train in the exposed, unforgiving style demanded by meadow combat — no cover, long sight lines, everything decided by strength and endurance. The yaksha veterans who run it have a simple philosophy: you learn to take a hit, and then you learn to give one back harder.

outcome.text: 'We can teach two things. Once each. Make your choices.'
The veteran returns to drilling her students.

animal_ocean_town_weapons.title: Town
animal_ocean_town_weapons.text: A trading post built into a sea cliff and expanded outward on platform structures above the tideline. Karka shell-wrights and naga-forged spear merchants dominate the market. The clang of metalwork reaches out into open water. Most things for sale here were made to puncture something.

outcome.text: You push through to the main stalls.
You skirt the settlement along the reef.

animal_ocean_town_magic.title: Town
animal_ocean_town_magic.text: A settlement built around a thermal vent, where the rising current brings strange minerals and stranger ideas. Water mages and naga sorcerers work from alcoves along the main tunnel. The air smells of sulfur and concentration. Someone is always arguing about the nature of current.

outcome.text: You find the practitioners' quarter.
You leave the argument unresolved.

animal_ocean_town_supplies.title: Town
animal_ocean_town_supplies.text: A market platform on stilts above the tidal flat. Everything needed to survive the reef and deep water — preserved food, medicine, rope, breathing equipment. The sign reads: WHAT YOU NEED. NO QUESTIONS. The price is printed underneath, which saves time.

outcome.text: The shopkeeper nods without looking up.
You keep going.

animal_forest_town_weapons.title: Town
animal_forest_town_weapons.text: A market at the forest's edge where different territories agree, briefly, to exchange. Dura shell-wright craftsmanship, vanara jugaad improvisation, shardula-claw handles on daggers sold by gana traders who got them somewhere no one is explaining. The weapons here are practical and tell stories.

outcome.text: You push through the stalls.
You skirt the settlement and continue into the trees.

animal_forest_town_magic.title: Town
animal_forest_town_magic.text: A forest settlement where the mycelium network runs under every building and the practitioners who use it for communication have built a small trade in that adjacency. Alchemy, earth magic, summoning — the disciplines that grow from understanding what is underground. The shelves smell of soil and something fermented.

outcome.text: You find the practitioners' stalls.
You leave the forest scholars to their arguments.

animal_forest_town_supplies.title: Town
animal_forest_town_supplies.text: A clearing settlement where four game trails meet. Sounder matrons and herb-walkers tend most of the stalls. Food preserved in bark and clay, medicines extracted from things most travelers walk past without recognizing, tools for the deep forest. It is honest trade in a place that doesn't demand credentials.

outcome.text: The matron at the nearest stall sizes you up and names a fair price.
You keep walking. The smell of drying herbs follows you down the trail.

animal_meadow_town_weapons.title: Town
animal_meadow_town_weapons.text: An armorer's compound at a crossroads of migration routes, built low and solid to survive the open-ground seasons. Dura shell-wright work alongside yaksha-enchanted blades and khadga-horn handles. The merchants here have traveled to get here and priced accordingly. Everything for sale is worth carrying a long way.

outcome.text: You find the weapons hall.
You continue across the open ground.

animal_meadow_town_magic.title: Town
animal_meadow_town_magic.text: A settlement gathered around a yaksha standing stone, which functions as both landmark and practice anchor. Enchantment, earth magic, white healing — the disciplines that thrive in open country where the sky is visible and the earth is close. The practitioners here are travelers themselves, stopping as they always stop.

outcome.text: You find the practitioners' quarter around the standing stone.
You leave the stone to its practitioners.

animal_meadow_town_supplies.title: Town
animal_meadow_town_supplies.text: A trading post at the great watering hole, where the migration routes converge and every creature passes through eventually. The merchants here have learned not to ask where anyone is going. Essential goods for the long traversal: food for crossing open ground, medicine for what open ground does to you, equipment for what you find at the end of it.

outcome.text: The shopkeeper glances up briefly and goes back to counting stock.
You keep moving. The watering hole glitters to your left.

events._comment_domain_guilds: === DOMAIN GUILDS — animal realm special locations ===

naga_palace.title: The Naga Palace
naga_palace.text: A coral arch rises from the reef, inscribed with naga glyphs marking territorial sovereignty. Two naga warriors flank the entrance but do not move to stop you. Beyond the arch, chambers of living coral lit by bioluminescent algae descend into the deep. Water magic and enchantment traditions have been practiced here without interruption since before the reef was reef.

outcome.text: A court official receives you with formal courtesy. They have everything the ocean's magic traditions offer. The price is calibrated to what you can pay, which means they already know.

choices.text: Observe the court protocol and withdraw respectfully

outcome.text:
You bow in the naga manner — low, without breaking eye contact — and withdraw. The court watches. A minor official nods very slightly.

You have not been insulted. In naga terms, this is an achievement.
You turn and leave the arch behind. The two warriors watch you go without expression.

ancient_banyan.title: The Ancient Banyan
ancient_banyan.text:
No one told you the tree existed, but you found it anyway. The banyan's aerial roots form a labyrinth; its canopy covers a quarter mile in every direction. The Vanara Elder sits in the first great fork, weaving something from spider silk and what you eventually realize is solidified starlight.

The tree has the attention of something older than itself. Earth magic and summoning traditions have always known about this place.

choices.text: Approach the Elder and ask to study

outcome.text: The Elder looks down from the fork with unhurried eyes. She names a price for her teaching. It is not small.

choices.text: Sit beneath the roots in silence

outcome.text: You sit with your back against a root as wide as a wall and close your eyes. The tree breathes. You breathe. After a time — you cannot say how long — something shifts: a sense of patience that is not your own, accumulated over centuries, seeping in through the bark.

choices.text: Walk away from the ancient tree

outcome.text: You leave the labyrinth of roots behind. The canopy covers you until you are out of the grove, and then the light returns all at once.

termite_cathedral.title: Termite Cathedral
termite_cathedral.text: The mound rises fifteen feet, engineered with an architect's precision for temperature and airflow. Carved archways mark the entrance in a script older than any living tradition. Inside, something hums at a frequency felt in the chest rather than heard by the ear. Yaksha practitioners and bhramara allies have used this place as a center of earth-consciousness work for as long as the mound has stood.

outcome.text: A yaksha practitioner emerges from the main chamber. Earth magic, summoning, and the basics of alchemy — the cathedral has all three. She names the prices plainly.

choices.text: Leave an offering at the base of the mound

outcome.text: You set your offering at the carved archway and stand back. The hum shifts frequency very slightly — just once. You take that as acknowledgement.
The hum follows you for longer than the mound is visible.

birds_congress.title: Conference of the Birds
birds_congress.text:
The great assembly tree rises alone on a ridge where forest meets meadow — visible from both territories, which is why it was chosen. Every bird of the realm comes here when the season is right. Kapota and shyena roost three branches apart in a truce older than memory.

A kapota elder calls the session to order with a chant that names every species present. You recognize the structure: a congress, a parliament. They are looking for something. They are, in the old story, always looking for the Simurgh. And, in the old story, they are the Simurgh — but they haven't arrived at that part yet.

choices.text: Attend the congress and learn from the teachings

outcome.text: A kapota messenger escorts you to an observer's perch. Air magic, space magic, and the white traditions of the sky practitioners — all available. The price is a story you haven't told anyone else.

choices.text: Listen to the full session without speaking

outcome.text:
You sit at the base of the tree for the full congress — hours, perhaps longer. The birds speak in twenty overlapping languages and you understand almost none of it.

But near the end, when the elder names the purpose of the journey, you understand that part. Not the words — the shape of it. The search that finds itself.

choices.text: Leave the birds to their congress

outcome.text: You descend from the ridge. The chant continues behind you, diminishing into the wind.

bone_forest.title: The Bone Forest
bone_forest.text:
The bones are organized, not scattered. Skulls face east, spines curve north, limb bones arranged radially from the center as though following a diagram. Something has been doing this for a very long time. In the center of the clearing, a practitioner in dark robes performs a slow ritual over a fresh death — a khadga, enormous, at peace.

They don't look up when you approach.

'Looking for death lessons,' they say. 'Or life ones. They're the same here.'

outcome.text: The practitioner rises, unhurried. Black magic and summoning — the traditions that work with what remains. They name the spells and the prices without ceremony.

You take your position across the body from the practitioner and mirror their movements as best you can. The ritual has its own grammar; you improvise where you don't know the words.

The khadga's presence, enormous even in death, seems to hold still for a moment. Then it passes, as presences do.
You bow toward the center of the bone arrangement and leave without disturbing anything. The practitioner has already returned to their work.

animal_sigh_of_relief.title: The Great Stag
animal_sigh_of_relief.text:
In a forest clearing — or on an open hillside, or at the edge of the reef where the light reaches — you find a great stag standing alone. His rack is hung with orchids. Around him, smaller creatures have gathered: a rabbit, two kapota pigeons, a young vanara sitting cross-legged. The stag is lowering his head, letting them feed from the flowers and mosses growing between his antlers.

No one has asked him to do this. He simply knows it is time.

choices.text: Meditate in the presence of this

outcome.text:
You settle into stillness. The stag's attention moves over you once, and then returns to the gathered creatures. That moment of attention is enough — something clear passes through you and keeps going.

You remember that generosity is not sacrifice. It is just knowing it is time.

choices.text: Leave some of your food for those gathered

outcome.text:
You set down what you can spare and step back. The vanara reaches it first, then shares without being asked.

The stag watches. He has seen this before — the chain of giving. It always surprises him a little.

You stay at the edge of the clearing and watch until the stag lifts his head and the gathered creatures drift away. Then the clearing is just a clearing again.

You carry the image of it for a long time.

choices.text: Approach and take from what is being offered

outcome.text:
You walk into the clearing. The gathered creatures scatter. The stag raises his head and looks at you with amber eyes.

He does not move. He does not attack. He simply regards you until you leave.

You feel, for a long time afterward, that you have been recognized.

animal_crossroads_shrine.title: Crossroads Shrine
animal_crossroads_shrine.text: Where three animal trails cross, someone built a cairn of stones. Prayer flags, thread, feathers pressed flat between layers of bark, bones arranged with obvious care — offerings that don't specify any particular tradition but cover their bases. A single butter lamp burns in a notch in the topmost stone.

outcome.text: You add something of yours to the cairn. The butter lamp flickers once in still air.

choices.text: Sit for a moment and breathe

outcome.text: You sit at the base of the cairn. At a crossroads, all directions are valid — this is what makes them sacred. For a moment you remember all of them.
You leave the lamp to its burning.

animal_ocean_naga_greeting.title: The Naga's Greeting
animal_ocean_naga_greeting.text:
A naga rises from the reef ahead — long, scaled, regarding you with amber eyes that haven't blinked. She circles once, slowly, then stops with her coils wound loosely around a pillar of coral.

'You are not of this water,' she says. It is not quite a question.

She is assessing you. This happens every time something new arrives in the ocean realm. She does not find it alarming — only relevant.

choices.text: Introduce yourself and explain your purpose

outcome.text:
You speak plainly. She listens without interrupting, which is the naga equivalent of a warm welcome.

When you finish, she unwinds from the coral pillar and gestures toward the open water. 'The western currents carry the faster trade. The eastern ones are watched.' She does not explain by whom.

You have been received.

You hold her gaze without flinching. She is silent for a long moment.

'Ah,' she says finally, and uncoils. She seems, somehow, pleased. 'The quiet ones always know where they're going.'

She examines the gift with the patience of someone for whom time is elastic. Then she accepts it.

In return, she describes three things: where the food is, where the danger is, and where the old temple lies. You did not ask about the temple. She offers it anyway, as though it were simply the correct exchange.

animal_karka_reef_warden.title: Reef Warden
animal_karka_reef_warden.text:
The pass through the coral barrier is narrow and long. Halfway through, a karka fills it completely — shell the width of the passage, claws braced against the coral walls, eyes fixed on you.

She is not sleeping. She has been watching since you entered the corridor.

The thermal vent behind her produces a faint heat that rises through the passage. This is her vent. This is her pass. These things are not in question.

outcome.text:
You speak to her in terms she respects — this is her territory, you acknowledge it; you need to pass, you explain why; you will not return unless invited.

Her eyes do not change. But after a long pause, she steps aside — just enough. The passage is tight. She watches every inch of it.

choices.text: Offer gold as a crossing toll

outcome.text:
She looks at the gold. She looks at you. She reaches out one claw and takes it with surprising delicacy.

Then she moves aside. The passage is yours. She adds the gold to a pile you hadn't noticed — there is a system here, practiced over years. You are not the first to find this more efficient than the alternative.
She braces. Her claws score the coral walls. Whatever comes next, she will not move from this vent.

You back out of the passage the way you came. There are other passes — you will find them.

Behind you, the karka returns to her vigil without comment. This happens, too.

animal_ridge_predator.title: Ridge Predator
animal_ridge_predator.text:
The pass through the thorn ridge narrows to a ledge barely wide enough to walk single file. At its midpoint, something large sits very still.

A shardula — a leopard of immense size, pale as the rock, watching you from exactly the spot the path must cross. His tail moves once, slowly. He does not rise.

He is neither blocking nor permitting. He is simply here, as he has been here many times before, watching what comes through.

choices.text: Make the formal greeting between predator-kin

outcome.text:
You lower your gaze, expose your throat briefly, and then meet his eyes again without aggression — the grammar of predator recognition. It takes composure you didn't know you had.

He considers this for a long moment. Then he stands, turns, and walks to the edge of the ledge, leaving the path clear. He watches you cross without looking away.

choices.text: Proceed slowly, making no threatening gesture

outcome.text:
You walk forward with the deliberate calm of something that does not consider itself prey. Each step measured. Gaze steady.

He watches the whole crossing. When you reach the other side, he blinks once — slowly — and looks away. You have been assessed and found unremarkable. In predator terms, this is the best outcome.

choices.text: Set down some food and step back

outcome.text:
You set a portion of food on the rock and retreat two steps. He looks at the offering, looks at you, and then — with the total lack of embarrassment of something that does not require gratitude — takes it.

The path is yours.
He rises from the rock in one fluid motion. His ears flatten. He has done this before.

animal_boss_simha_king.title: The King of Beasts
animal_boss_simha_king.text:
The oldest part of the forest is where he sits — where the trees are so wide you could sleep in their roots and the canopy blocks all direct sun. The simha king does not rise when you approach.

He is the largest lion you have ever imagined possible. His mane is the color of old wood. He is already ancient in legends that are themselves old. The portal to the Human Realm shimmers behind him in the roots of the oldest tree.

He is not blocking it, exactly. He is simply here, as he has always been here — at the threshold, at the end of the animal realm, where the path changes.

His gaze crosses your party without hurry, taking careful measure.

outcome.text:
You approach slowly and bow — low and long. When you rise, he has not moved, but something in his posture has changed: the calculation has left it.

'You have learned something here,' he says, in a voice like the ground settling. 'Go forward. Don't waste it.'

He stands and walks aside. The portal is clear.

choices.text: Offer tribute worthy of a king

outcome.text:
You present what you have with the ceremony the moment deserves. He examines it without touching it — not the goods, but the gesture.

'Adequate,' he says. He steps aside without further ceremony. 'The realm of humans is expecting something. Try not to disappoint it.'

He rises slowly — no urgency, no anger. He has simply agreed to your terms. His voice carries one last note before the charge:

'Good. I wanted to see if you could.'

choices.text: Attempt to find another way through

outcome.text:
You study the roots, the shadows, the angles. There is a gap — not much of one, but enough.

As you slip through, his voice reaches you from the center of the clearing: 'Clever. But you'll find cleverness has limits, further on.'

He does not pursue.
